correctness.rationale: At time n the urn contains n+1 balls; while X_n=x>0 the white/right probability equals (n+2-x)/[2(n+1)] <= 1/2 and conditional mean equals (n x+1)/(n+1). With s_n=P(T>n), a_n=E[X_n 1_(T>n)], the exact killed identity (n+1)a_(n+1)=n a_n+s_n telescopes to n a_n=1+sum_(k<n)s_k, with s_1=a_1=1. A common-uniform path coupling bounds subsequent survival by a simple symmetric walk absorbed at zero. Reflection gives Q_m(x)=P(-x<S_m<=x)<=min(1,2x/sqrt(m)). Hence s_(2n)<=2 n^(-3/2)(1+sum_(k<n)s_k). Starting from s_n=O(n^-1/2), applying the inequality yields O(n^-1), then O(log(n)n^-3/2), a summable tail, then O(n^-3/2). Summation yields E T<infinity and E T^theta<infinity for 0<theta<3/2, not a matching lower bound or endpoint result. The accompanying source exact-fraction checker is finite corroboration.
residual_risks: The survival exponent 3/2 is a proven upper bound, not sharpness, no statement about E[T^(3/2)] or second/multidimensional return.
